latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Active SARS-CoV-2 replication in upper and lower respiratory tract epithelium via ACE2-mediated entry; drives initial symptoms, transmissibility, and seeds downstream inflammatory and endothelial injury
SARS-CoV-2 antagonizes type I IFN signaling; impaired/delayed IFN response in genetically or autoantibody-predisposed hosts permits high viral burden and predicts severe disease

Dysregulated innate and adaptive immune activation driven by viral PAMPs and damaged epithelium; hallmark of the second-week deterioration with elevated IL-6, CRP, ferritin, and clinical hyperinflammation

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Alveolar epithelial type I/II pneumocyte injury
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Direct cytopathic injury to alveolar epithelium with loss of surfactant production and barrier integrity; substrate for diffuse alveolar damage and bilateral ground-glass opacities
Exudative phase with hyaline membranes, alveolar edema, and microvascular injury producing severe V/Q mismatch and refractory hypoxemia; pathologic substrate of severe/critical COVID-19 pneumonia

Direct viral and immune-mediated injury to pulmonary endothelium with endothelial swelling, complement activation, and microvascular dysfunction; couples viral replication to immunothrombosis and disproportionate hypoxemia
Cytokine-driven activation of coagulation, NETosis, platelet activation, and endothelial dysfunction producing pulmonary microthrombosis, in situ pulmonary thrombosis, VTE, and elevated D-dimer
Apoptosis, sequestration, and exhaustion of CD4/CD8 T cells; profound and persistent lymphopenia is a robust severity and mortality predictor
Combination of demand ischemia, microvascular injury, cytokine-mediated cardiac inflammation, and rare direct viral myocarditis producing troponin elevation and reduced LV function
Multifactorial AKI from hemodynamic injury, cytokine-mediated tubular injury, microthrombosis, rhabdomyolysis, and direct ACE2-mediated renal infection in severe disease
ACE2 expression in olfactory sustentacular cells leads to acute anosmia/ageusia; relatively specific in pre-Omicron era, less prominent with Omicron lineages
ACE2-mediated infection of intestinal enterocytes producing diarrhea, nausea, and prolonged fecal viral shedding

Combined effect of epithelial injury, lymphopenia, immunosuppressive therapy (steroids, IL-6 inhibitors), prolonged ICU stay, and broad-spectrum antibiotics increases risk of bacterial pneumonia, candidemia, and CAPA (COVID-associated pulmonary aspergillosis)

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Direct cytopathic infection of alveolar pneumocytes by replicating virus is the proximal trigger of epithelial injury
PAMP and DAMP signaling from infected/damaged cells drives downstream cytokine activation; high early viral load predicts severe inflammatory phase
Inadequate type I IFN signaling fails to restrict viral replication, prolongs viremia and amplifies severity
Infection of ACE2-expressing olfactory sustentacular cells produces sudden anosmia/ageusia
Enterocyte ACE2 supports intestinal infection and clinical GI symptoms
Cytokine flux activates endothelium and amplifies viral endothelialitis
Severe epithelial injury combined with surfactant loss and exudative edema produces diffuse alveolar damage
Endothelial injury contributes to exudative alveolar edema and microvascular dysfunction characteristic of COVID ARDS
IL-6/TNF activation, NETosis, and complement drive hypercoagulability and microthrombosis
Endothelial injury exposes prothrombotic surface and activates local coagulation cascade
Cytokine-driven apoptosis and tissue sequestration deplete circulating T cells
Systemic inflammation with demand ischemia and microvascular injury produces type 2 MI and troponin elevation
Cytokine-driven tubular injury and hemodynamic perturbation contribute to AKI in severe COVID
Profound and prolonged lymphopenia compromises adaptive defense against secondary infections
Viral replication drives pyrogen release and febrile response
Airway epithelial infection produces cough as a cardinal early symptom
Systemic viral cytokine response produces diffuse myalgia and fatigue
Fatigue is a prominent early and persistent symptom
Headache is a frequent early systemic symptom
Detectable PCR positivity is a direct marker of replicating virus
Higher viral load lowers Ct value (inverse relationship)
Antigen positivity correlates with high replicating viral load
Sustentacular cell injury produces sudden hyposmia/anosmia
Concurrent gustatory neuroepithelial injury produces dysgeusia/ageusia
Enterocyte infection produces diarrhea and nausea
IL-6 drives hepatic CRP synthesis; CRP rises with severity
Direct marker of the IL-6-dominant cytokine state
Hyperferritinemia accompanies hyperinflammatory phase; very high values raise concern for HLH-like state
Hyperinflammation and direct viral effects produce profound lymphopenia
Direct expression of the lymphopenia mechanism
Tissue injury releases LDH; elevation tracks lung injury severity
D-dimer is a direct marker of activated fibrinolysis from pulmonary microthrombosis and hypercoagulability
Acute phase fibrinogen elevation; consumption only in late DIC-like states
VTE and pulmonary thrombosis incidence is markedly elevated, particularly in ICU patients
Severe V/Q mismatch and shunt produce hypoxemia, often disproportionate to dyspnea
P/F ratio is the standard severity index of ARDS
Tachypnea reflects increased work of breathing and hypoxemia
Bilateral peripheral ground-glass opacities are the imaging signature of COVID alveolar injury
Crazy-paving and consolidation pattern reflects progression to organizing/exudative DAD
DAD pathway directly drives the ARDS event hazard
Severe DAD/ARDS drives intubation requirement
Troponin rise marks myocardial injury and tracks mortality
Direct expression of cardiac injury event hazard
AKI manifests as rising creatinine
Oliguria is a common manifestation of severe COVID AKI
Direct AKI hazard elevation in severe and critical disease

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Procalcitonin typically remains low/normal in pure COVID; significant elevation suggests bacterial coinfection
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Mild PCT rise possible in severe COVID; marked rise suggests superinfection
Susceptibility translates into hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia, candidemia, CAPA
Refractory hypoxemic respiratory failure is the dominant proximal cause of COVID-19 death
Pulmonary thrombosis and major VTE contribute to mortality independently of ARDS severity
Myocardial injury is an independent predictor of death
AKI requiring RRT is associated with high in-hospital mortality
Hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia and CAPA are major contributors to late mortality

axes.shape_free_text: Rises in first 1-3 days, often persistent for 5-10 days; biphasic in some patients with fever recurrence at day 7-10 with hyperinflammatory phase
axes.second_peak: Possible second fever peak day 7-12 with hyperinflammatory phase

axes.shape_free_text: Patient-reported or documented fever history when an exact temperature is not available; common in acute COVID-19 but can be absent.
Normal early; rises sharply if hypoxemia develops, often abruptly between day 5-10
Normal early; can drop precipitously between day 5-10; 'silent hypoxemia' common with SpO2 <90% disproportionate to symptoms
Mild tachycardia early with fever; marked tachycardia in severe disease
Maintained until late critical disease; falls in distributive/septic shock or with mechanical ventilation
Dry cough is a cardinal early symptom; persists 2-4 weeks
May be mild despite hypoxemia in acute COVID-19, but becomes prominent with pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, or ARDS.
Prominent throughout the course and persists into post-acute phase
Diffuse myalgia in early viral phase, usually resolves by day 7-10
Common early systemic symptom
Sudden hyposmia/anosmia, often without nasal congestion; high specificity in pre-Omicron era, less prominent with Omicron
Concurrent with anosmia in most cases
Variable; may precede respiratory symptoms
May reflect pleuritic/pericardial inflammation, myocardial injury, or pulmonary embolism in severe disease
Positive from day -2 (presymptomatic) through day 10-14; can persist longer in immunocompromised
Positive during phase of high viral load; insensitive in early presymptomatic and late phases
Low Ct (high viral load) early; rises with viral clearance; persistent low Ct in immunocompromised hosts
Falls early; nadir during hyperinflammatory phase; depth and persistence track severity
Often normal or low early; neutrophilia in severe disease, especially with bacterial superinfection
Rises with severity and bacterial superinfection; high N/L ratio is a severity marker
Mild thrombocytopenia common; severe thrombocytopenia signals DIC-like state
Rises sharply day 5-10; magnitude tracks severity; sustained elevation despite treatment suggests progression
Rises with hyperinflammation; high values predict need for ICU and mortality
Hyperferritinemia accompanies severe disease; markedly elevated values raise concern for HLH-like phenotype
Rises in proportion to lung injury; sustained elevation predicts respiratory failure and mortality
Rises through the inflammatory phase; very high values (>3-6 μg/mL) predict thrombosis and mortality
Acute phase elevation typical; falls only in late DIC-like states
Mildly prolonged in severe disease; marked elevation suggests hepatic injury or DIC
Elevation in severe disease tracks myocardial injury; independent predictor of mortality
Rises with AKI development in severe disease
Tracks AKI and prerenal contribution
Mild-moderate elevation common (2-5x ULN); higher values may reflect drug hepatotoxicity (remdesivir, paracetamol)
Often elevated in parallel with ALT and CK in severe disease
Elevated in severe disease and rhabdomyolysis
Typically low/normal in pure COVID; significant elevation suggests bacterial superinfection
Elevated in critical illness, shock, and severe respiratory failure
Declines with severity; hypoalbuminemia is a poor prognostic sign
Standard severity index of ARDS; <300 mild, <200 moderate, <100 severe
Bilateral, peripheral, basal-predominant ground-glass opacities; hallmark of COVID-19 pneumonia
Crazy-paving and consolidation appear with progression to organizing/exudative DAD
Total lung involvement summarizing GGO + consolidation; correlates with severity
Ordinal: 0 none, 1 nasal cannula, 2 simple/non-rebreather mask, 3 HFNC/NIV, 4 IMV, 5 ECMO; central determinant of which therapeutics are indicated
Time since symptom onset; primary modifier of antiviral efficacy (must be early) and corticosteroid timing (must be at hyperinflammatory phase)
Ordinal vaccination/boost status; major modifier of severity risk and pre-existing immunity
Severity of immunosuppression (transplant, hematologic malignancy, B-cell depletion, HIV with low CD4, high-dose steroids); modifies viral clearance and treatment selection
Variant susceptibility to anti-spike monoclonal antibodies; near-complete resistance for most pre-Omicron and Omicron-targeted mAbs across current circulating lineages
Risk from ritonavir-mediated CYP3A4 inhibition (statins, calcineurin inhibitors, anticoagulants, antiarrhythmics, etc.)
eGFR-based severity used to dose-adjust nirmatrelvir, contraindicate molnupiravir relative considerations, and adjust remdesivir; eGFR <30 contraindicates standard nirmatrelvir dose
Modifies remdesivir and nirmatrelvir use
Concurrent serious bacterial/fungal/TB infection; contraindicates IL-6 inhibitor and JAK inhibitor use
Pregnancy contraindicates molnupiravir and modifies risk-benefit of nirmatrelvir/r and immunomodulators
Rises in second week as DAD develops
Rises with severe ARDS
Markedly elevated in hospitalized and critical patients
Rises with severity, especially in ICU patients
Rises with hyperinflammation and critical illness
Rises with prolonged ICU stay, immunosuppressive therapy, and broad-spectrum antibiotics
Falls with AKI and shock
Concentrated between day 10 and day 28 in severe/critical disease; tracks combined ARDS, thrombosis, AKI, myocardial injury, and superinfection contributions

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Profound persistent lymphopenia is an independent predictor of mortality after adjusting for other inflammatory markers
Threshold-dependent rise in thrombotic risk with markedly elevated D-dimer; informs intensified anticoagulation decisions
Both downstream of the IL-6 axis; tightly linked in severe disease
Elevated LDH tracks lung tissue injury and predicts respiratory failure
Hypoxemia despite supplemental oxygen drives intubation
Troponin elevation is an independent mortality predictor
AKI requiring RRT is associated with very high in-hospital mortality
Significantly elevated PCT in COVID raises probability of bacterial coinfection
P/F ratio below 300/200/100 defines mild/moderate/severe ARDS by Berlin criteria
Tachypnea reflects compensation for hypoxemia and increased work of breathing

treatments.drug_class: SARS-CoV-2 Mpro protease inhibitor + CYP3A4 booster

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Mortality and hospitalization benefit observed when initiated within 5 days of symptom onset; minimal benefit later in non-immunocompromised hosts
Designed for outpatient mild-moderate disease; not established for those already requiring oxygen for COVID
Dose reduction required for eGFR 30-60; standard regimen contraindicated at eGFR <30
Ritonavir CYP3A4 inhibition produces life-threatening interactions with many cardiovascular, immunosuppressant, and antiarrhythmic drugs
Highest absolute benefit in high-risk and immunocompromised outpatients

failure_modes: Delayed initiation beyond viral replication window
treatments.context_specific_role: Outpatient antiviral for high-risk early COVID-19; requires strict early-window timing and DDI screening

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Greatest benefit within 7-10 days of symptom onset, before mechanical ventilation
Limited benefit once on mechanical ventilation; recovery time benefit largest in patients on low-flow oxygen
ALT >5x ULN warrants treatment hold; hepatic injury is dose-related
Extended courses considered in immunocompromised hosts with prolonged viral replication

treatments.context_specific_role: IV antiviral for hospitalized patients requiring low-flow oxygen, ideally within 7-10 days of symptom onset; also used in early outpatient 3-day regimen for high-risk

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Initiation within 5 days of symptom onset
Embryofetal toxicity in animal studies; contraindicated in pregnancy and during conception planning

failure_modes: Lower efficacy than nirmatrelvir/r in head-to-head comparisons
Cannot be used in pregnancy or pediatrics
treatments.context_specific_role: Alternative oral antiviral when nirmatrelvir/r and remdesivir are contraindicated or unavailable; lower efficacy than nirmatrelvir/r

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Mortality benefit demonstrated only in oxygen-requiring patients (RECOVERY); harm signal in non-hypoxemic patients
No benefit and possible harm in patients not requiring oxygen
May impair clearance of bacterial/fungal coinfection; requires concomitant antimicrobial coverage if suspected
Risk of further immunosuppression and prolonged viral replication

failure_modes: Use in non-hypoxemic disease (no benefit, potential harm)

side_effects.interpretation: Steroid-induced hyperglycemia, requiring insulin in many

treatments.context_specific_role: Cornerstone immunomodulatory therapy for hypoxemic hospitalized COVID-19; do not use in non-hypoxemic patients

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Benefit demonstrated in patients on oxygen with rapidly progressing disease, especially in hyperinflammatory state
Highest benefit when CRP markedly elevated (e.g., >75 mg/L)
IL-6 blockade may worsen untreated bacterial/fungal/TB infection
ALT >5x ULN is a relative contraindication due to hepatotoxicity
Profound neutropenia precludes use

failure_modes: Delayed administration after intubation in advanced fibroproliferative phase

side_effects.interpretation: Suppression of CRP synthesis confounds infection monitoring

treatments.context_specific_role: IL-6R blockade for severe COVID with rapidly worsening hypoxemia and high inflammatory markers, typically as add-on to dexamethasone

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Mortality benefit in hospitalized hypoxemic patients (COV-BARRIER, ACTT-2)
Active untreated serious infection contraindicates JAK inhibitor
Dose adjustment required at eGFR <60; not recommended at eGFR <15

side_effects.interpretation: Risk of bacterial/fungal infection and viral reactivation

treatments.context_specific_role: Alternative or additional immunomodulator to tocilizumab in hospitalized hypoxemic COVID-19

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Active bleeding or very high bleeding risk precludes pharmacologic prophylaxis; consider mechanical prophylaxis
Severe thrombocytopenia (<50) is a relative contraindication
Use UFH or dose-adjust LMWH at low CrCl

treatments.context_specific_role: Routine VTE prophylaxis for all hospitalized COVID-19 patients without contraindication

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Therapeutic-dose heparin reduces progression in hospitalized non-ICU patients (mpRCT) but lacks benefit and trends harm in ICU patients
No benefit and increased bleeding in critically ill ICU patients
Highest benefit in non-ICU patients with elevated D-dimer
High bleeding risk precludes therapeutic anticoagulation

failure_modes: Bleeding events in critically ill patients

side_effects.interpretation: Bleeding risk increased over prophylactic dosing

treatments.context_specific_role: Therapeutic-dose anticoagulation in hospitalized non-ICU patients with elevated D-dimer; not recommended in ICU patients

treatments.drug_class: Oxygen therapy (nasal cannula / mask / HFNC / NIV)

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Indicated for SpO2 <92-94% on room air; HFNC/NIV preferred at higher oxygen requirements

failure_modes: Failure of HFNC/NIV requiring escalation to mechanical ventilation
Self-induced lung injury from high spontaneous tidal volumes
treatments.context_specific_role: First-line supportive therapy for hypoxemia; HFNC reduces intubation need compared with conventional oxygen

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Severe ARDS or fatigue/altered mentation requires intubation; lung-protective ventilation (low Vt, plateau ≤30) and prone positioning when P/F <150

treatments.context_specific_role: Rescue therapy for severe ARDS; lung-protective ventilation with prone positioning is standard

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Mortality benefit demonstrated in moderate-severe ARDS; in non-intubated, awake proning improves oxygenation but mortality benefit less clear

failure_modes: Inability to tolerate due to obesity, agitation, recent surgery
treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunctive maneuver in moderate-severe ARDS, intubated and awake forms

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Most monoclonals (bamlanivimab, casirivimab/imdevimab, sotrovimab, bebtelovimab, tixagevimab/cilgavimab) lack activity against currently dominant variants; use only when local variant susceptibility is confirmed
Pre-progression early outpatient window
Highest absolute benefit when active product available against circulating variant

failure_modes: Variant resistance is the dominant mode of failure

side_effects.interpretation: Generic infusion reaction risk; not COVID-specific marker

treatments.context_specific_role: Variant-dependent option for early outpatient COVID, especially in immunocompromised; check local variant susceptibility before use

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: PCT elevation supports bacterial coinfection; without it, routine antibiotic use is discouraged
Use only when bacterial coinfection is suspected on clinical/microbiologic grounds

failure_modes: Routine empiric use in unselected patients drives resistance and Clostridioides difficile risk
Delayed coverage of multidrug-resistant pathogens in late HAP/VAP

side_effects.interpretation: C. difficile and resistant organism selection

treatments.context_specific_role: Targeted use only when bacterial coinfection is suspected; not routine for COVID alone

age_lt_50.trajectory_modulation: Lower risk of severe disease and ARDS; mortality typically <0.5% in unvaccinated

age_65_74.trajectory_modulation: Markedly higher hospitalization and ICU rates

age_ge_75.trajectory_modulation: Highest mortality risk; case fatality 5-20% in unvaccinated cohorts

bmi_ge_30.trajectory_modulation: Increased ARDS, mechanical ventilation, and mortality risk

bmi_ge_40.trajectory_modulation: Class III obesity is among strongest non-age severity factors

present.trajectory_modulation: Worse glycemic control and inflammatory state predict severe disease and mortality
Often confounded with age and obesity but remains an independent severity risk

ckd_stage_3_or_4.trajectory_modulation: Increased AKI, mortality, and constraints on therapeutic options

esrd_dialysis.trajectory_modulation: Highest non-transplant CKD risk; profoundly elevated mortality

copd.trajectory_modulation: Higher hospitalization and respiratory failure risk

ild.trajectory_modulation: Markedly higher progression to severe disease

present.trajectory_modulation: Higher rates of myocardial injury and mortality

solid_tumor_recent_chemo.trajectory_modulation: Higher mortality, especially with active treatment

hematologic_malignancy.trajectory_modulation: Highest mortality and prolonged viral shedding, especially after B-cell depletion

transplant_recipient.trajectory_modulation: Prolonged viral shedding, blunted antibody response; favors antiviral and ongoing virologic surveillance

anti_cd20_therapy.trajectory_modulation: Severely impaired B-cell response; persistent viremia and chronic COVID phenotype

pregnant_third_trimester.trajectory_modulation: Higher risk of severe disease, ICU admission, and preterm birth

primary_series_only.trajectory_modulation: Substantial protection against severe disease, waning over months

boosted_within_6_months.trajectory_modulation: Largest reduction in severe disease and mortality risk

prior_infection_within_12_months.trajectory_modulation: Hybrid immunity (infection + vaccination) provides strongest protection against severe disease

male.trajectory_modulation: Slightly higher mortality and ICU admission rates

supportive_care: VTE prophylaxis with prophylactic-dose LMWH for all hospitalized patients without contraindication
Lung-protective ventilation (low tidal volume 6 mL/kg PBW, plateau pressure ≤30 cmH2O) and prone positioning when P/F <150 in intubated ARDS
Awake prone positioning for non-intubated hypoxemic patients tolerating the maneuver
Glycemic control during dexamethasone therapy with sliding-scale or basal-bolus insulin as needed
Stress ulcer prophylaxis in critically ill patients on mechanical ventilation or coagulopathy
Vigilant monitoring for bacterial and fungal superinfection (CAPA, candidemia) in immunosuppressed and ICU patients
Conservative fluid management once initial resuscitation complete, given propensity for pulmonary edema
Early mobilization and physical therapy when oxygenation permits to reduce ICU-acquired weakness
Nutritional support with enteral feeding preferred
Empiric strongyloides screening or ivermectin in patients from endemic regions before high-dose steroids
Latent TB consideration before prolonged steroid + biologic immunosuppression
Isolation precautions per institutional protocol; airborne precautions for aerosol-generating procedures
Mental health support and recognition of post-ICU syndrome and post-COVID symptoms during convalescence
Pulse oximetry monitoring at home for selected outpatients with risk factors and clear escalation criteria
Discharge planning with anticoagulation reassessment, follow-up imaging if persistent symptoms, and rehabilitation referral
